name: Hanoi
summary: Hoan Kiem Lake and the Old Quarter's street food, Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum, the Temple of Literature and Hoa Lo Prison, with Ha Long Bay and Trang An a day trip away.

months.note: Cool, grey and drizzly; trips and prices rise ahead of Tet in late Jan or Feb.
Tet (Lunar New Year) usually falls here; many shops close for days and transport sells out.
Mild and humid with misty drizzle; pleasant for walking the Old Quarter.
Warm spring weather; the 30 Apr–1 May holidays bring domestic crowds.
Hot, humid start to the wet season with afternoon storms.
Very hot and humid with heavy downpours.
Peak heat and rain; storms from typhoons in the region are possible.
Wettest month; plan indoor backups and expect street flooding.
Rain eases late in the month; 2 Sep National Day brings domestic travel.
Autumn is one of the best times to visit: drier, warm and clear.
Dry and comfortable; peak season for Hanoi and Ha Long Bay.
Cool and dry; bring a jacket for evenings.

tips.title: 90-day e-visa for all nationalities
tips.body: Vietnam's e-visa allows stays of up to 90 days from your declared entry date, with single or multiple entry. The state fee is USD 25 for single entry and USD 50 for multiple entry, and it is non-refundable. Apply only on the official portal, evisa.xuatnhapcanh.gov.vn.

tips.title: 45-day visa-free entry for 12 countries
tips.body: Citizens of Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the UK, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland can stay up to 45 days without a visa. This exemption under Resolution 44/NQ-CP runs from 15 March 2025 to 14 March 2028. For a longer stay, get the 90-day e-visa.

tips.title: ASEAN visa-free stays
tips.body: Ordinary passport holders from Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia and Laos get 30 days visa-free. Philippine citizens get 21 days, and citizens of Brunei and Myanmar get 14 days.

tips.title: Your hotel registers you with police
tips.body: Accommodation providers must report foreign guests to local police within 12 hours of arrival. Hotels usually do this at check-in using your passport. If you stay in a private home, make sure the host registers you.

tips.title: Train Street is officially off-limits
tips.body: Commercial activity on Hanoi's Train Street has been banned since October 2019, and tour operators have been told not to bring visitors there. Hanoi has called all cafe activity there a violation, and in February 2026 the authorities agreed to run fewer passenger trains and stop freight trains on this stretch. The only sanctioned viewpoint is the Hoa Xa cafe inside Long Bien Railway Station.

places.name: Hanoi Old Quarter
places.blurb: Dense grid of trade-named streets north of Hoan Kiem Lake.

places.name: Dong Xuan Market
places.blurb: Hanoi's largest covered market, in the north of the Old Quarter.

places.name: Hoan Kiem Lake
places.blurb: Central lake with Turtle Tower and Ngoc Son Temple.

places.name: Ngoc Son Temple
places.blurb: Temple on an islet in Hoan Kiem Lake, reached by the red The Huc Bridge.

places.name: Ma May Ancient House
places.blurb: Restored 19th-century merchant tube house in the Old Quarter.

places.name: Bach Ma Temple
places.blurb: One of Hanoi's oldest temples, on Hang Buom Street.

places.name: O Quan Chuong Gate
places.blurb: The last surviving gate of Hanoi's old city walls.

places.name: Long Bien Bridge
places.blurb: Early-1900s steel cantilever bridge over the Red River.

places.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
places.blurb: Granite mausoleum holding Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body, on Ba Dinh Square.
places.tip: Mornings only; closed Mondays and Fridays. Cover shoulders and knees.

places.name: Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House
places.blurb: Grounds of the Presidential Palace, with the simple stilt house where Ho Chi Minh lived.

places.name: One Pillar Pagoda
places.blurb: Small 11th-century-origin pagoda raised on a single stone pillar.

places.name: Vietnam Military History Museum
places.area: Ba Dinh (old site) / Nam Tu Liem (new site)
places.blurb: National museum of Vietnam's military history, associated with the Hanoi Flag Tower.
places.tip: The museum moved to a new building on Thang Long Boulevard in late 2024: check the address before you go.

places.name: Tran Quoc Pagoda
places.blurb: Hanoi's oldest pagoda, on a small peninsula in West Lake.

places.name: Vietnam Museum of Ethnology
places.blurb: Museum of Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups, with full-size traditional houses outdoors.

places.name: Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre
places.blurb: Theatre for traditional water puppetry, by Hoan Kiem Lake.

places.name: Temple of Literature
places.blurb: 11th-century Confucian temple and site of Vietnam's first national university.

places.name: St. Joseph's Cathedral
places.blurb: Neo-Gothic cathedral from 1886.

places.name: Hoa Lo Prison Relic
places.blurb: Museum in the remaining gatehouse of the French-built prison later called the 'Hanoi Hilton'.

places.name: Hanoi Opera House
places.blurb: French colonial opera house from 1911; the interior is open only for performances.

places.name: Ta Hien Beer Street
places.blurb: Old Quarter street of bia hoi stalls and bars around Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen.

places.name: Perfume Pagoda
places.area: My Duc, about 60 km SW of Hanoi
places.blurb: Buddhist cave-temple complex reached by boat and a short hike.

places.name: Hanoi Train Street
places.blurb: Narrow residential strip with cafes where trains pass inches from homes.
places.tip: Officially off-limits: Hanoi has banned business on the tracks since 2019 and cut train services in Feb 2026. The sanctioned view is from the cafe inside Long Bien station.

places.name: Cafe Dinh
places.blurb: Upstairs cafe off Hoan Kiem Lake, known for egg coffee.

places.name: Bun Cha 74 Hang Quat
places.blurb: Lunch-only Old Quarter shop for bun cha and crab spring rolls.

places.name: The Railway Hanoi
places.blurb: Trackside cafe on Train Street.

places.name: Cha Ca Thang Long
places.blurb: Restaurant serving cha ca, Hanoi's turmeric-dill fried fish.

places.name: Phung Hung Mural Street
places.blurb: Railway viaduct arches painted with murals of old Hanoi.

places.name: Pho Gia Truyen
places.blurb: Long-running beef pho shop with a queue-and-pay system.

places.name: Imperial Citadel of Thang Long
places.blurb: UNESCO-listed former royal citadel, including wartime command bunkers.

places.name: Cong Caphe
places.blurb: Retro-themed Vietnamese cafe chain, known for coconut coffee.

places.name: Banh My Tram
places.blurb: Small shop for Hanoi-style pate banh mi.

places.name: Quan Thanh Temple
places.blurb: Taoist temple near Truc Bach Lake with a large bronze statue.

places.name: Ca Phe Duy Tri
places.blurb: Long-running cafe known for yogurt coffee.

places.name: Banh Cuon Ba Xuan
places.blurb: Old Quarter stall for steamed rice rolls.

places.name: Bun Bo Nam Bo Bach Phuong
places.blurb: Shop on Hang Dieu serving bun bo nam bo, a dry beef noodle salad.

places.name: Ha Long Bay
places.area: Quang Ninh, about 170 km E of Hanoi
places.blurb: UNESCO-listed bay of limestone karsts, visited by day trip or overnight cruise.

places.name: Trang An
places.area: Ninh Binh, about 90 km S of Hanoi
places.blurb: Karst landscape explored by rowing boat through caves and rivers.

places.name: Bun Cha Huong Lien
places.blurb: Bun cha restaurant known for the 2016 Obama and Bourdain meal.

places.name: Pho 10 Ly Quoc Su
places.blurb: Michelin Guide-listed beef pho shop near the cathedral.

places.name: Pasteur Street Brewing Co.
places.blurb: Taproom of a Vietnamese craft brewery.

places.name: Tam Vi
places.blurb: One-Michelin-star restaurant for northern Vietnamese home cooking in a vintage setting.

places.name: The Lighthouse Sky Bar
places.blurb: Old Quarter rooftop bar with city and Red River views.

places.name: Cafe Giang
places.blurb: Family cafe credited with inventing egg coffee.

places.name: SWI:P Speakeasy Bar
places.blurb: Hidden cocktail bar.

places.name: Old Quarter View Hanoi Hostel
places.blurb: Social Old Quarter hostel with free breakfast and a free-beer hour.

places.name: Hanoi EcoStay

places.name: Capella Hanoi
